basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 3-5.' and it opens 'VERS. 3-5.-- Et reversae sunt aquae de terra euntes | et redeuntes. Dum dicitur: Reversae'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 3-5.-- Et reversae sunt aquae de terra euntes | et redeuntes. Dum dicitur: Reversae sunt aquae de terra euntes et redeuntes, videtur, juxta litteram, quia omnes fluviorum ac rivorum decursus per occultas terrae venas ad matricem abyssi redeunt, juxta illud Salomonis: Ad locum unde exeunt flumina, revertuntur, ut iterum fluant (Eccle. I, 7).
